cohort: Women with twin pregnancies delivered at 24-40 weeks of gestation between 1995 and 2014 (n=1614)
finding: While second-born twins overall had higher rates of adverse neonatal outcomes, this was primarily driven by lower birth weight; however, second twins delivered due to early-preterm and late-preterm PROM had higher risks of RDS and mechanical ventilation support, respectively, even after adjusting for birth weight.
birth_weight: Birth weight was recorded and used in the analysis.
